## Exit criteria

| ID | Check | Requirements | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| E22 | kea perfdhcp numbers are documented for one Tenko node: 4-way exchanges and renewals per second and the p99 from DISCOVER to ACK, every lease committed to the store before its ACK, on loopback and from the load VM over a real link, with and without metrics | DHCP-17, DHCP-07, OPS-21 | - |
| E23 | The reference home-lab environment runs DHCPv4 through Tenko for all four networks: the gateway relays each network to one Tenko node, giaddr and option 82 select the scope, clients keep their addresses across the switch, option 6 and option 42 reach them, and the rollback is one setting on the gateway | DHCP-01, DHCP-02, DHCP-04, DHCP-15 | - |
| E24 | Leases survive the node: the node is killed (SIGKILL, and a power-off of the lab VM) under perfdhcp load and restarted, no lease that was acknowledged is lost, no address is leased to two clients, and the role's lease table equals the store's rows; while the store refuses writes (the test hook of WP6.2) the role behaves as P3-Q14 decides | DHCP-07, OPS-02, OPS-26 | `crates/tenko-dhcp/tests/lease_crash.rs` |
| E25 | The five-device move lab of Phase 1 (E8) runs with the DHCP step automatic for the `reserved` devices: the reservation in the target scope from IPAM intent, the observation from the new lease without polling, the old reservation and lease removed in the cleanup, the `static` device stopping at its manual step, the rollback on a blocked step | IPAM-19, DHCP-16, IPAM-18, CON-10 | `crates/tenko-ipam/tests/move_dhcp.rs`<br>`crates/tenko/tests/acceptance_move.rs`<br>`crates/tenko/tests/acceptance_move.rs::e25_the_dhcp_step_is_automatic_for_reserved_devices_and_a_lease_confirms_the_move` |
| E26 | A client with option 81 and a legacy client that sends only option 12 get their A and PTR records and a DHCID in Tenko zones on ACK, the records go on release and on expiry, and a second client that claims the first one's name is refused by name protection (RFC 4703); the profile defaults of P3-Q6 hold | DHCP-13 | `crates/tenko/tests/acceptance_dhcp_ddns.rs` |
| E27 | The relay and options lab: four networks in compose behind a relay; giaddr and link selection (RFC 3527) choose the scope, option 82 is echoed, a shared network with two subnets fills both, options inherit from server to scope to class to reservation, vendor class, user class and MAC wildcard classes select policies, a MAC deny list and an allow list on a restricted scope hold, a squatter is detected before the offer, a DECLINE quarantines the address, and a BIOS, a UEFI and a UEFI HTTP client boot over PXE (iPXE in QEMU) | DHCP-01 to DHCP-06, DHCP-08, TGL-16, TGL-17 | `crates/tenko-dhcp/tests/conflict.rs::lab_m35_squatters_are_skipped` |
| E28 | The reconciliation view shows the four truths (intent, leases, DNS records, scans) for the lab data with the ghost, rogue, orphan and PTR-mismatch lists and the "who wins" rule of each, and a lease's options 55 and 60 set the OS field of an unmanaged host | IPAM-21, DHCP-14, IPAM-23 | `crates/tenko/tests/acceptance_reconcile.rs`<br>`crates/tenko/tests/acceptance_reconcile.rs::e28_the_view_lists_every_seeded_case_and_a_lease_sets_the_os_of_an_unmanaged_host` |
| E29 | DHCPv6 through a relay in the lab: IA_NA from a pool, IA_PD from a delegation pool, a DUID reservation from IPAM intent, RFC 6939 correlation with the DHCPv4 lease of the same MAC, the names of RFC 4704, and the M and O flag check of DHCP-10 in the health view | DHCP-09, DHCP-10, DHCP-11, DHCP-13 | - |
| E30 | The Kea JSON export of the lab configuration and its leases is accepted by `kea-dhcp4 -t` and `kea-dhcp6 -t`, and a Kea server started from it hands the exported reservations to their clients | MIG-16 | - |
| E31 | Fuzz targets for the DHCPv4 and DHCPv6 wire formats, the option parsers and the relay information run in the weekly fuzz smoke | API-14, API-15 | - |
| E32 | Idle RSS below 100 MB with every role including `dhcp` serving the home scopes, on the musl binary, one node; metrics overhead on the DORA path below 2 percent; the memory of 100,000 leases measured | OPS-15, OPS-21 | - |
| E33 | Validation from the lab root: a name in a zone signed by Tenko and one in a zone signed by BIND answer with AD through a DS chain from the lab root's trust anchor (NSEC and NSEC3, a wildcard, an opt-out delegation, NODATA and NXDOMAIN proofs); a bogus zone (a DS that matches no key, a wrong signature, an expired signature) answers SERVFAIL with the extended error of RFC 8914 that names the fault, and the same name with CD set answers its data with AD clear; an unsigned zone under a signed parent answers with AD clear and no error; a negative trust anchor for the bogus zone lets it through, with its audit record, and stops letting it through when it expires | DNS-13, OPS-09 | - |
| E34 | An RFC 5011 roll of the lab root's KSK (a new key published, the hold-down time passed, the old key revoked) is followed by the node without an operator: the new anchor is Valid in the trust anchor table before the old one is revoked, the state changes are audited, and validation never fails during the roll; a node started from a backup taken before the roll follows it on start | DNS-13 | - |
| E35 | On the wire: the lab TLD's query log shows only the labels QNAME minimisation sends for a name three labels below it, never the full name; after one NXDOMAIN whose NSEC (and, in the NSEC3 zone, whose NSEC3) covers a range, a second name in that range is answered NXDOMAIN with no query to the authority (the authority's log shows none), the same for NODATA and for a wildcard; names below a cached NXDOMAIN are NXDOMAIN (RFC 8020) | DNS-34 | - |
| E36 | Priming at start from the shipped hints and from a hints file, and again before the root NS set expires; the resolver survives, within its work budget and with SERVFAIL and the extended error that names the cause: a lame delegation, a delegation whose name servers point at each other without glue, a CNAME loop, a TLD whose servers do not answer, a server that breaks 0x20, one that answers FORMERR to EDNS, one that truncates everything, and a referral with out-of-bailiwick glue; the failure of each is cached per RFC 9520 and the counts of queries sent are documented | DNS-03, DNS-08 | - |
| E37 | resperf and dnsperf against the lab root from the load VM, on the musl binary, cold cache and warm, with and without validation: resolutions per second at a fixed latency budget documented (M36, M37, M38) | DNS-03, DNS-27 | - |
| E38 | Idle RSS below 100 MB with every role, the home zones, a full answer cache and the infrastructure cache after a run of 100,000 distinct names, on the musl binary, one node; the infrastructure cache stays within its bound | OPS-15 | - |
| E39 | The Internet smoke, observational: the owner's networks resolve through Tenko alone with no upstream for a day (a DoT root rule kept ready as the one-command fallback), the AD zone forwarded to the domain controllers, validation on; the dashboard's SERVFAIL share, p50 and p99, cache hit ratio and sub-query counts are recorded; then the owner-run switch of section 9 | DNS-03, DNS-13, DNS-02, TGL-22 | - |
| E40 | Fuzz targets for every new parser of network data (referrals and glue, DNSKEY, DS, RRSIG, NSEC and NSEC3 in the validator, the trust anchor file) run in the weekly fuzz smoke; the counting-allocator test still binds steps 1 to 7 of the query path, now with a validated cache hit, a hit for a client without DO, a hit on a bogus entry and a synthesised NXDOMAIN | API-14, API-15 | - |
| E41 | The RPZ triggers NSDNAME and NSIP, which a forwarding resolver cannot match ([dns-resolver.md](../dns-resolver.md) section 5.2), match in the lab for a name whose delegation the resolver followed | DNS-21 | - |
| E42 | The conformance rows this plan adds to CONFORMANCE.md are Implemented or Partial with test references, and the exit document records every criterion's state | API-17 | - |
